  Introduce a sample-ordering bug, save a failed named case, reproduce the

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{3. Record, replay and fix a failure}

```{r options, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
```

Suppose a test fails on a colleague's machine. A replay record identifies the
case, source revision, fixture checks, R seed and observed environment. With
the matching source and inputs, you can rerun the case and compare the failure.
It does not bundle the source or install old R/package versions for you.

We will deliberately introduce the sample-ordering bug from the
[first tutorial](biocroxytest.html), record it, replay it and fix it. This uses
the named cases from [the memory/HDF5 tutorial](named-cases.html), but all setup
is repeated here so the article can be run independently. Use the GitHub
development version and the dependencies listed in the first tutorial.

## Start from the example package

```{r copy-package}
template <- system.file("examples", "samplealignment", package = "biocroxytest",
                        mustWork = TRUE)
pkg <- tempfile("samplealignment-")
fs::dir_copy(template, pkg)
source_file <- file.path(pkg, "R", "align-samples.R")
named_source <- system.file("examples", "steps", "named-cases.R",
                            package = "biocroxytest", mustWork = TRUE)
file.copy(named_source, source_file, overwrite = TRUE)
withr::with_dir(pkg, biocroxytest::use_longtests())
```

The case `sample-alignment/memory` asks for `s3, s1` and expects counts
`31, 11` and conditions `treated, control`. We will run only that case here.

## Introduce a specific bug

The correct implementation selects columns by name:

```r
align_samples <- function(x, samples) x[, samples]
```

Replace it with a membership check. `%in%` keeps columns in their original
order, so requesting `s3, s1` incorrectly returns `s1, s3`. The following
block edits only that function line, preserving all the test assertions:

```{r introduce-bug}
correct <- readLines(source_file)
broken <- correct
broken[startsWith(broken, "align_samples <-")] <-
  "align_samples <- function(x, samples) x[, colnames(x) %in% samples]"
writeLines(broken, source_file)
```

## Run and record the failure

```{r run-failure, message=FALSE}
roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg)
id <- "sample-alignment/memory"
failed <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = id, seed = 42L)
failed$cases[c("id", "status")]
cat(failed$cases$detail, "\n")
```

The status should be `failed`. The diagnostic identifies three mismatches:
sample names, counts and conditions. The backend check still passes.
`run_test_plan()` returns the report so you can inspect or export failures;
use `check_test_plan()` when failures must stop a CI job.

```{r verify-failure, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(failed$cases$status, "failed"))
```

## Save and replay it before editing the source

```{r replay}
record_file <- tempfile("alignment-failure-", fileext = ".rds")
record <- biocroxytest::write_test_replay(failed, id, record_file)
replayed <- biocroxytest::replay_test_case(record_file, path = pkg)
replayed$comparison$same_failure
```

The result should be `TRUE`: the failure's condition types, messages and
available source locations match. `record$command` provides a command for
replaying from the source package's root. The explicit `path = pkg` above
lets us stay in our current working directory.

Keep the record **outside the package directory**, as we do here. Otherwise
saving it could change the source fingerprint. Export requires a failed case
and a new output filename. Keep the matching faulty source if you want to
replay it again after fixing the package.

Replay restores the recorded base R seed and selected environment settings.
Inspect `replayed$comparison$environment_changes` for differences. Matching
R and dependency versions, external services and backend-specific random
streams still need to be managed separately.

```{r verify-replay, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(isTRUE(replayed$comparison$same_failure))
```

## Fix the function and keep the regression test

Restore name-based selection and run the same case against the corrected
source. This is a new test run: replay intentionally requires the original
source revision.

```{r fix, message=FALSE}
writeLines(correct, source_file)
fixed <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = id, seed = 42L)
biocroxytest::check_test_plan(fixed, required = id)
fixed$cases[c("id", "status")]
```

The case should now be `completed`, and `check_test_plan()` should return
without an error. We changed only the function body, so the generated test
assertions remain current. If you edit a declaration, regenerate it first.
Commit the corrected source and its generated regression test.

You have now seen the same expected result protect sample order in an ordinary
test, across two backends, and through failure replay. Continue with
[verified fixture files](test-fixtures.html), [CI recipes](test-workflows.html),
or [two historical Bioconductor regressions](bioconductor-regressions.html).
The [paired-data reduction recipe](reduce-failures.html) is an optional next
step when the data needed to reproduce a failure are too large.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
if (isNamespaceLoaded("samplealignment")) unloadNamespace("samplealignment")
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)
unlink(record_file)
```
